# react-native-viewport-detector

> Detect when a view enters the viewport in React Native. Works inside ScrollView, FlatList, FlashList and nested horizontal lists (visibility is clipped by every ancestor scroll container). Event-driven: no timers while idle, one batched check per scrolled frame. API mirrors the web's react-intersection-observer. Pure JS: works in Expo Go, old and new architecture, iOS and Android. React 18+, React Native 0.72+.

Install: `npm install react-native-viewport-detector`

## Core API

- `<ViewportProvider rootMargin? pauseWhenInactive?>` — wrap exactly one scrollable (ScrollView, FlatList, FlashList, Animated.ScrollView). Required for scroll tracking. Nest providers for nested scroll views.
- `useInView({ threshold?, rootMargin?, triggerOnce?, delay?, skip?, initialInView?, onChange?, root? })` → `{ ref, inView, entry }` (also `[ref, inView, entry]`). Attach `ref` to a host View.
- `<InView ...sameOptions ...ViewProps>{children | ({ inView, entry }) => node}</InView>` — a View that tracks itself; with plain children + `onChange` it never re-renders.
- `useViewportRoot({ rootMargin? })` → `{ ref, scrollProps, Provider, invalidate, handle }` for lists that cannot be wrapped.
- Jest: `import { setupViewportMock, mockAllInView, mockInView, resetViewportMock } from 'react-native-viewport-detector/jest'`.

## Canonical usage

```tsx
import { ScrollView, View } from 'react-native';
import { ViewportProvider, useInView, InView } from 'react-native-viewport-detector';

<ViewportProvider>
  <ScrollView>{items.map(item => <Row key={item.id} item={item} />)}</ScrollView>
</ViewportProvider>

function Row({ item }) {
  const { ref, inView } = useInView({ threshold: 0.5, triggerOnce: true });
  return <View ref={ref}>{inView ? <Content item={item} /> : null}</View>;
}

// impression: visible ≥ 1 s, once
<InView threshold={0.5} delay={1000} triggerOnce onChange={v => v && track(item.id)}><Ad /></InView>
```

## Rules

- No `<ViewportProvider>` → measured against the window and not updated on scroll (dev warning). Use `root={null}` for static screens.
- `threshold` is area-based (0–1). `rootMargin` is pixels; on the outermost provider it extends past the screen (preload).
- For which FlatList rows are visible, `onViewableItemsChanged` is enough; use this library for arbitrary views and nested lists.
- 1.x `ViewPortDetector`/`ViewPortDetectorProvider` are deprecated (still work); see docs/MIGRATION.md.

## Benchmark (vs alternatives, Android emulator + iOS simulator, 300 rows)

Rows reported wrong while scrolling (Android / iOS): this library 8–10% / 8%, react-native-intersection-observer 24–27% / 26%, react-native-viewport-detector 1.x 26% / 33–34%, @futurejj/react-native-visibility-sensor 116–200% / 110–112%. Same frame cost as no tracking on an idle host. Details: docs/BENCHMARKS.md.
